items.comparator: For the reported selectivity result, the source says it rose from 51.82% to 85%; no separate control or comparator is stated. For the specialty-chemicals yield result, the reported change is from 72% to nearly 90%; no separate comparator is stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: The original article says Mira “pushed a single-step reaction's selectivity from 51.82% to 85% in three months.” It also reports a specialty-chemicals project where the company says it “improved production yield from 72% to nearly 90%.”
items.signal: An AI system paired with an autonomous lab reportedly improved reaction selectivity and specialty-chemical production yield. The article describes a closed loop in which physical-test data trains the model; this could be a hard-to-copy capability if supported by repeatable, customer-validated results. Both outcomes are company-reported in a press-distributed article.
items.source: ACCESS Newswire article carried by Yahoo Finance

The announcement gives no measured performance result.

items.signal: Reported benchmark performance for a drug-discovery AI tool; a capability signal, not a demonstrated operating benefit in a pharmaceutical workflow.

Research collaboration pairs ASKA’s gynecological therapeutics expertise with Insilico’s proprietary PandaOmics AI target-identification engine; ASKA is to validate AI-predicted targets. Distinctive data access or exclusivity was not specified.

items.quantitative_outcome: The company said post-training Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on a proprietary scientific-data dataset improved performance beyond comparable closed models; exact numerical outcome: none stated.
items.signal: A reported use of proprietary scientific data to fine-tune an open model for protocol troubleshooting. The company described the benchmark but did not provide numeric results in the article.

items.company: Anthropic (with BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, and The Column Group)
items.comparator: For the reported CAR-T signaling-domain result, a standard signaling domain widely used in approved CAR-T products; the article says the candidate was about 70% shorter in amino-acid sequence. Other reported results used different metrics and conditions.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports a roughly 70% reduction in CAR-T signaling-domain sequence length, a 10× or greater antibody-affinity improvement in certain variants, and an 89% reduction in manufacturing-record review time. These are separate results; no single common comparator or controlled overall drug-development comparison is given.
items.signal: Reported AI-supported results across preclinical design and workflow tasks. The coverage cautions that results were mainly technical reports or preprints, not peer-reviewed findings, and do not establish a shorter overall development timeline or higher clinical success rate.

items.comparator: For smaller corporate borrowers, decision time described as changing from “weeks to minutes”; international borrowers from “months” to “weeks.” No quantified baseline or controlled comparison stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: “For smaller corporates, we're talking weeks to minutes.” For international borrowers, “months might turn into weeks.”
items.signal: AI-supported lending process reduces credit decision time; Reuters reports the bank said the system went live in summer 2026. The comparison is before/after processing time as characterized by a bank executive, without a study design or numeric duration.
items.source: Reuters, as reported by Yahoo Finance

items.comparator: No numerical or before/after comparison stated; the announcement describes additional private-company ownership data compared with relying solely on modeled ownership estimates.
items.signal: Partnership with Nasdaq Private Market to integrate capitalization-table data supported by “verifiable, auditable documentation and filings” into FactSet Workstation—a potentially differentiated source of private-market ownership data for investment research.

items.quantitative_outcome: The bank said its generative AI platform “had increased investigator productivity by about 40 percent.”
items.signal: Reported productivity gain for financial-crime investigators using its Newton generative-AI platform. The report says the bank did not disclose how the improvement was measured, so the comparator and measurement basis are unclear.

items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The report says the company completed all research milestones under a Phase I SBIR and collected and analyzed high-resolution foreign-object-debris imagery; it gives no measured operating outcome.
items.signal: Potential distinctive data-access move: Safe Pro says it developed an AI dataset using imagery of foreign-object debris encountered on U.S. Air Force and civilian airfields under an AFWERX SBIR. The source does not quantify dataset size or resulting detection performance.

items.comparator: L3Harris says its internal test environment; the source does not specify the test design or which frontier labs/models were compared.
items.quantitative_outcome: “In a few days we were able to outperform the frontier labs in our test environment and cut costs by 95%.”
items.signal: Early reported result from testing sovereign models on internal work using L3Harris enterprise data. The reported cost reduction and model-performance comparison are promising but company-reported and not accompanied by test details or independent validation.
items.source: Palantir company announcement quoting L3Harris Chief Transformation Officer Heidi Wood

items.comparator: A full year of manual penetration testing, according to the company’s account; test scope and methodology are not given in the article.
items.quantitative_outcome: “three weeks of model-assisted analysis matched a full year of manual penetration testing, with broader coverage,” according to Palo Alto Networks. The article also reports the company said AI models identified more than 14,000 previously undetected open-source vulnerabilities.
items.signal: Reported vulnerability-discovery throughput suggests a possible advantage in analysis scale. The claim is attributed to Palo Alto Networks and the article does not provide independently evaluated methods or results.
items.source: Economic Times, quoting Palo Alto Networks

items.comparator: A three-day exercise in which Armadin’s red-team swarm generated more than 33,000 alerts per day; no non-AI or prior-workflow baseline is stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: The company reports it “triaged every alert” and that “all 38 paths were reconstructed with evidence” during the three-day exercise; no comparative baseline or accuracy rate is stated.
items.signal: A high-volume live exercise is a potentially relevant workflow-scale signal for AI-assisted defense, but the account is published by TENEX itself and does not establish performance against a conventional workflow.

items.comparator: No baseline or control comparison stated; lab measurements at Deutsche Telekom’s Bonn lab and Nokia’s Oulu lab. Field validation is planned, not yet reported.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Initial lab measurements of AI-based uplink channel estimation demonstrated typical throughput improvements of 10–15%, with gains increasing as radio channel complexity increased.” The reported measure is uplink throughput; the release does not specify the comparison baseline.
items.signal: AI-based channel estimation produced a measured lab throughput improvement in telecom RAN processing. The result is preliminary and awaits field validation, but real-time channel estimation in a commercial RAN stack may be a capability with operational differentiation.

items.comparator: AI-managed beamforming trial results; the excerpt reports percentage improvements but does not state the baseline or control condition.
items.quantitative_outcome: “16% improvement in downlink user throughput, a 12% improvement in spectral efficiency and a 10% increase in downlink data volume.” Reported for New York City trials, especially during peak hours; comparison baseline not stated.
items.signal: Measured network-performance gains from AI-managed beamforming in a live-operator context. Potentially differentiated by the operator’s network conditions and deployment data, though the available report does not disclose the comparison methodology.

items.comparator: No measured baseline stated for the new Erlangen workflows; the headline figures are described as potential reductions or targets, not verified outcomes.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Up to 85 per cent less manual engineering effort” is identified by the report as a project target; no independently verified result for the new workflow is stated. Production-planning cost savings of up to 20% are also described as potential, not measured outcomes.
items.signal: The workflow combines product, component and bill-of-materials information with factory digital-twin and synthetic-image tools to prepare inspection before a physical prototype exists. The integration of Siemens’ product and production data could become distinctive, but the reported figures are targets rather than demonstrated operating benefits.
items.source: Robot Harbour, reporting on Siemens’ Erlangen factory work with NVIDIA
